sentences.text: She worked out the year over about two years, and she did it the boring way, which was photographs.

There are perhaps two thousand photographs of that farm in three boxes and a biscuit tin, and Elin went through all of them twice between the ages of eleven and thirteen, on the floor of the back bedroom, and told her mother she was doing a project.
The willow standing up gives you before January 2015.

The jetty with planks on it is harder; her father reckoned the planks came off in the late nineties and her grandmother said 1997 and there is a photograph from a christening in 1999 in which they are already gone.
And then she had the T-shirt, which is not much of a clue, and the boy, who was somebody's child on their own land in a valley of four farms.

She had ruled her uncle out on height and there were no other boys of that age in the valley in the nineties, which left one candidate and which she had known perfectly well from about the fourth second and had spent two years not looking at directly.
She got it in the end from a box in the back bedroom.
It is a photograph from the summer of 1994 of her father, aged eleven, on the end of that jetty, with his elbows on his knees, in a red T-shirt.
It is not the same moment.

She has been very careful about this and has looked at that photograph perhaps a thousand times: in the picture he is looking at the camera and slightly annoyed, and the boy she saw was looking at the reeds and was not annoyed at all.
It is the same afternoon, or the same fortnight, or the same summer.
It is not the same second.
Which matters, because the obvious explanation is that she saw the photograph as a small child, forgot it, and reassembled it on a hot afternoon at eleven.
Elin thinks that is probably what happened.
She has said so out loud to the two people she has told.
It accounts for the boy and the T-shirt and the jetty and even the willow, because the willow is standing up in about four hundred other photographs in those boxes.

What it does not account for is the second one, at thirteen, standing up, in which there was a bicycle on the grass — and there is no photograph of a bicycle by that jetty in any of the three boxes or the tin, and she has looked, and her father says he had a bicycle then and used to leave it exactly there.
Elin was thirteen when she worked it out and she did not tell anybody for nine years.
